A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PGPSE research. Their text, equations, figures, and complete Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including renamed environments and relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original gridworld experiments measuring exploration entropy, state coverage, dataset properties, and downstream offline Q-learning performance.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and appendix analyses, with revised offline Q-learning results in Figure 3.

M1.justification: PGPSE retains its joint entropy objective, per-agent policy gradients, and minibatch updates. Algorithm 1 is reformatted; its omitted softmax initialization remains documented in Appendix B. The parallel Frank–Wolfe algorithm is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Room and labyrinth gridworlds, their deterministic and stochastic variants, and downstream goal-reaching tasks. LAB becomes Maze, with corresponding label changes; no environment or task is added.

E2.justification: The matched-budget single-agent comparisons and random-policy dataset baselines remain unchanged. Adding Random to Figure 2's legend identifies an already evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Sections 6 and Appendices B–C retain the trajectory budgets, metrics, 10,000 training episodes, horizons of 8 and 10, and offline Q-learning settings. No protocol revision is reported to explain the changed Figure 3 values.

E4.justification: The four-agent comparison, stochastic-environment tests, occupancy heatmaps, goal-reachability maps, and policy-diversity analysis are retained. Their analytical questions and supporting appendix figures are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent runs, the same seed list, and the same mean/standard-deviation reporting for exploration and dataset entropy. Figure 3 still specifies five runs; no new uncertainty procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Figure 3 revises success-rate bars for parallel, single-agent, and random datasets in both deterministic environments. Several former 1.0 plateaus become values below 1.0, while the overall comparator ordering remains. Other empirical figures retain their results.

T1.justification: Appendix A corrects the entropy-component bound in Theorem A.1's proof: the inequality chain changes from ≤ to ≥ and max(p_i, 1−p_i) becomes min(p_i, 1−p_i). It also adds derivative-sign reasoning for the variance/entropy ratio. The theorem statements remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: parallel entropy maximization, concentration analysis, PGPSE, and benefits for exploration and offline learning. The added Takeaways box summarizes existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly explains that coordination supports specialization despite decoupled trajectories, distinguishing this setting from interdependent trajectories in conventional MARL. Existing interpretations and limitations concerning gridworld evaluation, scalability, and diminishing benefits from additional agents remain.

D1.justification: The code-access hyperlink changes from an anonymous.4open.science repository in Section 6 to an author-named GitHub repository in Appendix C. This changes the documented access destination; implementation details and hyperparameters are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds a focused comparison with shared-environment MARL, citing Albrecht et al., Li et al., Zhao et al., and Lupu et al. Zamboni et al. (2025) is also added. Other bibliography changes largely update publication information or consolidate duplicates.

P1.justification: V2 copyedits paragraphs, standardizes Room/Maze terminology, updates the running title and affiliation, and adds brief explanations and a takeaway. The section sequence and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2–3 move closer to their discussion and are enlarged; Figure 2 gains a Random legend entry, and Figure 3 identifies dataset types in its subcaptions. V2 also restyles explanatory boxes and Algorithm 1 and widens Figure 4, retaining the same figure set.

improvement.justification: The local proof correction in Appendix A improves mathematical consistency, while clearer MARL positioning and figure labels improve understanding. These are limited gains: the evaluation scope is unchanged, and the unexplained Figure 3 revisions do not establish stronger empirical support.
